item.dc:creator: Andrew Zaleski

item.title: New, Solar-Powered Safari EVs Are Getting Us Closer Than Ever to Wildlife
item.dc:creator: Greg Presto

item.title: I Hiked the Appalachian Trail with a Couple Weeks Before They Were Murdered
item.dc:creator: Earl Swift

item.title: What Really Happened on Broad Peak, the Deadliest High-Alpine Tragedy in More than a Decade
item.dc:creator: Ben Ayers

item.title: I Spent 24 Straight Hours at an Ultramarathon. Here’s Why Runners Go Long.
item.description: 100-Mile trail races booming in popularity, and every other person we know seems to be training for an ultra. Our writer—who is not a runner—wanted to understand why. So, he stayed up all night at California’s Western States Endurance Run interviewing athletes, race crew, and fans. Here’s what he learned.
item.dc:creator: Roman Stubbs

item.title: Noodling for Catfish Is Now a Tourist Activity. We Blame TikTok.
item.description: Once outlawed, hand-fishing for giant catfish in the Southeastern U.S. has never been more popular, thanks to viral videos on social media. We booked a tour with a noodling guide to see if the tug is really like a drug.
item.dc:creator: Aidan McCahill

item.title: This Veteran’s Cure for Soldiers with PTSD: Go Build an Earthship in the Desert
item.description: Ryan Timmermans, an Army veteran who did multiple tours in Afghanistan, invites former soldiers to live away from running water and the power grid in a self-sufficient community in Northern New Mexico. Timmermans believes the simple lifestyle is more therapeutic than anything the government can provide.
item.dc:creator: Nick Aspinwall

item.title: This State Will Pay You $12,000 to Move There—and the Mountain Biking Is World-Class
item.description: As housing costs spike nationwide, West Virginia is investing millions in trail networks and outdoor infrastructure, turning public lands, navigable rivers, and miles of singletrack into year-round tourism engines and an outdoor rec oasis for its residents.
item.dc:creator: Eric J. Wallace

item.title: Hot Pools, Waterslides, and Cocktails: Inside Therme’s Plan to Bring Supersized Health Spas to the USA
item.description: Therme Group, Europe’s wellness behemoth, is planning to open stadium-sized health spas across the USA. Are Americans ready for Roman baths? We traveled to Bucharest to find out.
item.dc:creator: Bill Gifford

item.title: What Can Athletes Learn From Courtney Dauwalter's Winning Streak? Joy Is More Powerful than Results.
item.description: What do the world’s best endurance athletes have in common? In his latest book, ‘The Way of Excellence,’ author Brad Stulberg explores the importance of positive emotions on training and racing.
item.dc:creator: Brad Stulberg

item.title: Low Water, No Problem. We Took a Packraft Down One of the Most Remote (and Stunning) Rivers in the West.
item.description: The Lower Owyhee River in eastern Oregon is remote, tough to access, and impossibly beautiful. Writer Owen Clarke recently tagged along on an packrafting trip down the river during its dry season.
item.dc:creator: Owen Clarke

item.title: The Enhanced Games Promised a Drug-Fueled Athletic Revolution. Then Things Got Messy.
item.description: Backed by tech billionaires, flooded with performance-enhancing drugs, and designed to smash records, the "Doping Olympics" finally arrived in Las Vegas. But the reality of sports without hypocrisy was a lot messier than advertised.
item.dc:creator: Joshua David Stein

item.title: Colorado’s Wolf Reintroduction Hasn’t Gone to Plan. Are the New Midnight Cowboys Its Last Hope?
item.description: In the name of wolf conservation, Colorado is reviving the cowboy way of life—starting with a team of 15 range riders. Not everyone’s happy to see them.
item.dc:creator: Corey Buhay

item.title: A Century Before Lewis and Clark, an Indigenous Explorer Traversed the Continent. I Spent a Year Studying His Adventure.
item.description: After a devastating personal loss, I spent a year tracking the clues of a 300-year-old mystery to show how a nearly forgotten Indigenous explorer reached the Pacific a century before Lewis and Clark.
item.dc:creator: Mike Bezemek

item.title: The Fierce Battle Over the True Height of Mount Rainier
item.description: Eric Gilbertson has a very particular set of skills. He climbs mountains all over the world, attempting to measure them more accurately than anyone ever has. But when he discovered that Mount Rainier was shorter than advertised, no one wanted to hear it.
item.dc:creator: Peter Frick-Wright

item.title: On the Camino de Santiago, José Andrés Recovers from the Weight of the World
item.description: One of the world’s most famous humanitarians has spent decades feeding millions in the wake of disaster via World Central Kitchen. Now, on an ancient pilgrimage across Spain’s Camino de Santiago, he is learning how to carry the weight of the universe one step at a time.
item.dc:creator: Kevin Sintumuang

item.title: She’s Funding Her 2,600-Mile PCT Hike with OnlyFans. Traditionalists Are Skeptical. She Couldn’t Care Less.
item.description: Kamryn Renae's Instagram account exploded after she began posting flirty videos from the PCT, clad in pink booty shorts and matching nail polish. She knows what she is doing.
item.dc:creator: Grayson Haver Currin

item.title: Two Texas Flood Victims Still Haven’t Been Found. These People Won’t Stop Looking.
item.description: Recovery teams descended on Texas' Guadalupe River in the wake of the 2025 floods. Their task was to locate the remains of the dead, to provide solace for the living. Almost a year later, some are still missing.
item.dc:creator: Ian Dille

item.title: I Spent a Week in the Jungle to Find Out Why Women Are Paying Thousands to Talk About Hormones
item.description: Could a week in the jungle rewrite the rules of menopause?
item.dc:creator: Christine Yu

item.title: Want to Climb the World’s Highest Peak? Mount Everest Training Is Anything But Easy.
item.description: How do climbers train their bodies to reach the summit of Everest? There’s lots of jogging, a few laps on a homemade ladder bridge, and maybe even a frigid climb in the middle of the night, for starters. These days, Everest coaches and training plans prepare a climber’s legs, lungs, and self-confidence for the rigors of the peak.
item.dc:creator: Frederick Dreier
